HM04-q01-cpsp57: Too close; explosives may never be parked within 5 feet of the traveled part of the road.
The shoulder can be within 5 feet of traffic lanes; staying with the truck does not make that legal.
HM04-q02-ldm4g9: The 300-foot list is bridges, tunnels, buildings, places where people gather and open fires, not empty rest areas.
An empty field is not on the 300-foot list; the rule protects bridges, tunnels, buildings, crowds and open fires.
HM04-q03-3fqo3v: Locked doors don't matter; an explosives vehicle may be left unattended only in a safe haven.
No time allowance exists; don't park on private property unless the owner knows the danger, and never leave it unattended there.
HM04-q04-vvpzk2: At a truck stop the vehicle must still be watched by you; others may watch it only on shipper, carrier or consignee property.
Flashers don't change the rule; someone else may watch it only on the shipper's, carrier's or consignee's property.
HM04-q05-30wic2: The sleeper berth does not count; the attendant must be awake in the vehicle or within 100 feet with a clear view.
250 feet is too far and a restaurant blocks the view; the limit is 100 feet with the vehicle in clear view.
HM04-q06-esiqk0: An empty Class 3 tank still holds vapor that a flare can ignite; never use flares near it, loaded or empty.
Fuses are burning signals too, banned near Class 3 or Division 2.1 tanks at any distance; use triangles or red electric lights.
HM04-q07-35xtsz: The shipper does not check your route; finding out about permits and special routes is the driver's job.
Police don't plan your trip; you, the driver, must find out about permits and routes before starting.
HM04-q08-5jjw49: Class 9 loads need no written route plan; that requirement is only for Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 explosives.
Weight alone does not trigger a written route plan; the rule covers Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 explosives.
HM04-q09-mw3wei: 5 feet is the explosives parking distance from the road; smoking is banned within 25 feet.
100 feet is the attending distance; the no-smoking distance is 25 feet.
HM04-q10-hx57bo: The engine must be turned off before fueling a vehicle that contains HazMat.
Someone must always be at the nozzle controlling the fuel flow; never walk away from it.
HM04-q11-pckl1o: Carrying two does not help; the one on the power unit must be UL rated 10 B:C or more.
No water-type rule exists; the handbook requires a UL rating of 10 B:C or more.
HM04-q12-po8cpj: Kicking or thumping a tire doesn't count; a tire pressure gauge is the only accepted way.
Looking at a tire can't measure pressure; only a tire pressure gauge is accepted.
HM04-q13-n1zk7c: The end of a trip is too late; examine every tire when a trip starts and every time you park.
Waiting until a tire looks low is too late; check at the start of each trip and each time you park.
HM04-q14-kwlpdl: Papers must stay where responders can find them, in the driver's door pouch or on the seat; you keep them only at an accident scene.
A locked glove box hides the papers; they belong in the driver's door pouch or on the driver's seat.
HM04-q15-deoqqb: Extra extinguishers are not the chlorine rule; you need an approved gas mask and a dome-fitting leak kit.
A survey meter measures radiation and is used after radioactive spills, not required for chlorine tanks.
HM04-q16-syx3l5: Cargo tanks used for HazMat must stop at crossings whether loaded or empty.
Any amount of chlorine requires a stop at railroad crossings, even a small amount.
HM04-q17-vcjf5k: 5 to 25 feet is too close; stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest rail.
50 to 100 feet is too far back; the rule is 15 to 50 feet from the nearest rail.
HM04-q18-3pjidu: Responders don't look up the shipper or date; the ERG is indexed by proper shipping name and ID number.
The carrier's DOT number is not how the ERG works; it is indexed by proper shipping name and ID number.
HM04-q19-h8vyng: Hot doors may mean a cargo fire; opening them lets in air and can make it flare up.
Even a crack lets in air; don't open hot doors, and don't fight HazMat fires without training.
HM04-q20-nf8oou: Never keep driving with HazMat leaking to find help; park, secure the area, stay and send someone.
Never repack leaking containers; call for help and keep people away instead.
HM04-q21-jizi5g: Never smell to identify a leak; toxic gases can destroy your sense of smell and kill you, even with no odor.
Never touch leaking material; identify it from the shipping papers, labels or package location.
HM04-q22-0nb221: Covering them is not enough; remove all explosives before separating and place them at least 200 feet away.
You don't wait for the shipper; remove the explosives before separating vehicles and place them at least 200 feet away.
HM04-q23-tqy7ze: A death as a direct result of a HazMat incident is on the list and requires a call.
A public evacuation of more than 1 hour is on the list and requires a call.
HM04-q24-0q0twx: 24 hours is how long the NRC and CHEMTREC lines are staffed; written reports are due within 30 days.
1 hour is the evacuation and road-closure trigger; the detailed written report is due within 30 days.
HM04-q25-7391tx: The 30-day written report is the carrier's report to CHEMTREC; a California highway spill must be reported immediately.
Injury is not required; any HazMat spill on a California highway must be reported immediately to CHP or police.
HM04-q26-glr7ul: CHEMTREC does not issue endorsements; it gives emergency crews technical information about HazMat.
Local authorities usually designate safe havens; CHEMTREC gives technical information about HazMat.
